slot.brief: A cycle composed of known segments (isobaric + isothermal/adiabatic) on a P–V diagram with numeric states; compute total work in cycle, heat in a branch, or efficiency using first law per branch.

stem: One mole of a monatomic ideal gas follows the cycle $A\to B\to C\to A$: $A\to B$ is isochoric, with pressure rising from $P_0$ to $2P_0$; $B\to C$ is isothermal expansion from $V_0$ to $2V_0$; $C\to A$ is isobaric at $P_0$. If $P_0V_0=100$ J, what is the cycle efficiency?

verdicts.working: States are A=(P0,V0), B=(2P0,V0), C=(P0,2V0). Net work is W=2P0V0 ln 2 − P0V0 = 38.6 J. Heat input is Qin=(3/2)P0V0 + 2P0V0 ln 2 = 288.6 J. Efficiency W/Qin = 13.4%.

working:
$W_{BC}=2P_0V_0\ln 2,\quad W_{CA}=-P_0V_0$.
$W_{\rm net}=100(2\ln 2-1)=38.6\ \text{J}$.
$Q_{AB}=\Delta U_{AB}=\dfrac{3}{2}P_0V_0=150\ \text{J}$.
$Q_{BC}=W_{BC}=2P_0V_0\ln2=138.6\ \text{J}$.
$\eta=\dfrac{W_{\rm net}}{Q_{AB}+Q_{BC}}=0.134=13.4\%$.

Independent check: States are A=(P0,V0), B=(2P0,V0), C=(P0,2V0). Net work is W=2P0V0 ln 2 − P0V0 = 38.6 J. Heat input is Qin=(3/2)P0V0 + 2P0V0 ln 2 = 288.6 J. Efficiency W/Qin = 13.4%.
solution:
For a complete cycle, $W_{\rm net}=W_{BC}+W_{CA}=100(2\ln 2-1)=38.6\,\text{J}$. Heat is absorbed during $AB$ and $BC$:
$$Q_{\rm in}=\frac{3}{2}P_0V_0+2P_0V_0\ln 2=288.6\,\text{J}.$$
Thus, $\eta=W_{\rm net}/Q_{\rm in}=0.134=13.4\%$.
